text:
jia: Heads-up — after HF->Redwood conversion for community-chat-1 we see subtle formatting regressions on the chat evals.

jia: Example: messages that used to preserve a leading space before code blocks are now concatenated. Short diff from logs:

jia: ```
input: 'Here's the snippet:\n    def foo():\n        return 1'
old_tokens: ['Here', ''s', 'Ġthe', 'Ġsnippet', ':', '\n', '\n', '\n', 'def', 'Ġfoo', '():']
new_tokens: ['Here', ''s', 'Ġthe', 'Ġsnippet', ':', '\n', 'def', 'Ġfoo', '():']
```

jia: So it looks like an extra prefix-space/whitespace pretokenization event was lost and indentation collapsed — causes downstream formatting fails in chat templates.

sahil: Hm. Two quick checks: 1) tokenizer normalizer config (NFC vs NFKC vs none) 2) byte_fallback / byte-level pretokenizer differences between HF fast vs the runtime. Did we load the tokenizer with use_fast or convert the tokenizer.json?

sahil: Many HF models rely on add_prefix_space=true for space-sensitive tokenizers (roberta/gpt2 variants) — if that flag toggled during conversion you'll see missing Ġ tokens.

emma: Also saw this in a quantized bring-up. Not the quantization itself, but small probability shifts interacting with beam/best-of heuristics made the model select a variant that assumes a different whitespace tokenization. Eval numbers: Rouge-L dropped ~2.1 pts on our chat formatting suite, and pass@1 for code formatting examples fell 18%.

jia: Repro steps I used:

jia: ```
# huggingface clone load
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('community-chat-1', use_fast=True)
print(t.backend_tokenizer.normalizer)
print(t.special_tokens_map)
print(t.init_kwargs.get('add_prefix_space'))
```

jia: On Redwood conversion we used our hf-to-redwood tool that generates a tokenizers.json and a slim config.json. I noticed the converted tokenizers.json had a 'sequence' normalizer step removed (it listed only lower-case in the original).

sahil: Can you paste the tokenizers.json normalizer block from the converted artifact? suspect it's switching from NFKC to "strip_accents" or dropping normalizer entirely. If normalizer->decompose/compose differs you'll get different byte sequences for same input.

jia: Pasted snippet:

jia: ```
"normalizer": {
  "type": "Sequence",
  "normalizers": [
    {"type": "NFC"},
    {"type": "Lowercase"}
  ]
}
```

jia: Original HF had NFKC + Strip + Lower.

emma: That explains it — NFKC can fold certain compatibility whitespaces and punctuation differently than NFC. Also if byte fallback (from the HF tokenizer) is implemented differently in our runtime (we had a bug where unknown bytes were replaced with the unicode replacement char instead of using byte-level escaping) you can lose leading spaces when they are represented as different codepoints.

sahil: Quick mitigation: convert tokenizer with exact normalizer sequence and ensure add_prefix_space preserved. In the conversion tool add a sanity check: compare tokenized text of a canonical set of prompts (our chat formatting probe) between HF python tokenizer and the generated runtime tokenizer. Fail the conversion if any mismatches.

emma: I can add a regression test. Proposed canonical probe cases:

emma: - leading space + code block
- multi-space indentation
- nbsp and other non-breaking spaces
- zero-width joiner sequences

ops-bot: deploy note: converted tokenizer v2.1.4 pushed to staging, traffic routing disabled until manual approval.

sahil: Other gotchas: special_tokens_map mismatch. HF sometimes stores '' but downstream templates expect "\n" or a custom <|endofturn|>. Make sure special tokens mapping survived conversion. Also ensure chat templates normalize whitespace in inputs before tokenization only if consistent with training.

jia: Action items: 
1) Emma add the canonical probe suite + fail-if-diff to hf-to-redwood pipeline.
2) Sahil add conversion guard to copy exact normalizer sequence and add_prefix_space flag.
3) Jia run full eval on quantized INT8 build to confirm regressions are gone after matching tokenizer.

emma: I'll open the PR with tests + a small util to compare token sequence diffs (printing offsets). Will attach sample failing inputs.

sahil: One more low-level tip — when using tokenizers v0.13 -> 0.15 the normalizer serialization changed shape a bit; conversion needs to support both. Also validate using both use_fast and use_slow HF implementations to catch discrepancies.

jia: Thanks. If anyone hits similar failures in other models, drop the probe inputs here and we'll expand the suite.

emma: :thumbsup:
